questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: How to write a formal job application
Why people send fewer emails than before
Rude emails at work and why people write them
How to use emojis in business messages
questions.why: They discuss what people find rude in emails and the psychology behind rudeness at work.

questions.q: What annoys Rachel in Manchester about some emails?
options: They are much too long and hard to follow
They start with only her name and no greeting
They are often sent very late at night
They are full of spelling and grammar mistakes
questions.why: Rachel dislikes emails starting with just her name, without a greeting like 'hi'.

questions.q: What did one anonymous listener receive in reply to a carefully written email?
options: A single emoji
No reply at all
A very angry message
A phone call
questions.why: Dr Peter Olusoga says they received a single emoji in response to a carefully worded email.

questions.q: How does Phil feel about getting a single emoji as a reply?
options: He thinks it's funny
He thinks it's a normal, friendly reply
He often does it himself
He says it would annoy him too
questions.why: Phil says, 'I think that would annoy me too.'

questions.q: According to some psychologists, what is rudeness in emails based on?
options: A fight-or-flight response when people are stressed
Poor writing skills learned at school
Differences between cultures and languages
Not knowing the other person very well
questions.why: Becca says rudeness in emails is based on a fight-or-flight response humans feel when stressed.

questions.q: Which is an example of the 'fight' response that Dr Emma Russell describes?
options: Not replying to an angry email at all
Answering only some of the points in the email
Copying in senior staff to put someone in their place
Waiting a whole day before replying
questions.why: She says fight includes hostile emails or cc'ing senior personnel to put someone in their place.

questions.q: What does Emma Russell say makes people more likely to be rude?
options: Working from home and feeling lonely
Being tired and stressed from doing too much
Using a mobile phone to reply quickly
Having a new boss who is very strict
questions.why: She says because we're all quite frazzled, we're more at risk of incivility.

questions.q: Why does Phil say pausing before you hit send 'might save your friendship or even your job'?
options: To joke that emails are not really important
To suggest people should stop using email
To show that bosses secretly read all emails
To show an angry email can have serious results
questions.why: He advises pausing when angry, because a rude email could cost you a friendship or a job.
